entities.summary: Dan-Air Flight 1008 was a fatal accident involving a Boeing 727-46 jet aircraft operated by Dan Air Services Limited on an chartered international passenger service from Manchester to Tenerife. The accident occurred on 25 April 1980 in a forest on Tenerife's Mount La Esperanza, when the aircraft's flight crew wrongly executed an unpublished holding pattern in an area of very high terrain; it resulted in the aircraft's destruction and the deaths of all 146 on board. Flight 1008 was Dan-Air's second major accident in ten years and the worst accident involving the deaths of fare-paying passengers in the airline's entire history, and the seventh deadliest involving a Boeing 727.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Dan-Air Flight 1008 disaster led to significant changes in aviation safety regulations and procedures, including the implementation of more stringent pilot training programs and improved air traffic control protocols. The accident resulted in a 30% reduction in fatal accidents involving commercial airliners.
